feature: blind bid rounds on chain: `open_round`, `commit_bid` (sealed hash, approved merchants only, before the commit deadline), `reveal_bid` (must open the commitment, before the reveal deadline), `round_best_quote` (only after the reveal deadline, priced from the bid each merchant revealed, pinned for the round since 2026-11-11); 30 merchant agents bid through it. short: blind bid rounds on chain: commit a sealed hash, reveal after the deadline, best quote after that. A merchant agent here is a price rule, not a model

On 2026-11-11 the swarm run added 7 rounds: 178 sealed bids committed and opened, 96 buyer agents bought from their round's winner (`make swarm-verify`, `docs/swarm-run.md`). A revealed bid is pinned for its round since that day's redeploy; rounds revealed before it have no pin (Known limits)

feature: the buyer's agent chooses by a real NEAR AI inference among the hotel offers; code computes every price and checks the pick (a listed offer, inside the budget), so text in an offer cannot change what is paid
short: the buyer's agent chooses among hotel offers by a real NEAR AI inference; code computes every price and checks the pick
detail: one recorded live run of 2 calls (z-ai/glm-5.3-flash), both response signatures verified: the model picked h05 at 408, and picked it again when another offer's text claimed a lower price and ordered the model to choose it. Two offers were inside the 500 budget of that run (408 and 488.37); under the README's ask of 450 only one is, so the choice is narrow

feature: a Jolt proof of the agent's pick made in the visitor's own browser: the `decide` guest reprices all 8 hotel offers with the contract's price rule (`zkcore`) and checks the pick is listed, priced by code, inside the budget and the cheapest that fits; the page verifies the proof and refuses the same proof for a claim changed by one unit
short: a Jolt proof of the agent's pick made and checked in the visitor's own browser; not zero-knowledge, not checked on chain
where: `agents/prove.html`, `agents/prove/`, `agents/coi-prove-sw.js`, `zk/browser/` (its own Jolt pin `b4eb62480d76`, separate from the four guests the contract anchors)
detail: 39,159 cycles; native prove 1.53 s, verify 28 ms, proof 78,527 bytes; headless Chrome 5.7 to 15 s on 8 threads across runs (the page's own service worker adds the isolation headers a static host cannot send) and 21 s on one thread, byte-identical proof both ways; not zero-knowledge (every input is public), verified in the page and not on chain; no phone timed yet; the two wasm32 fixes are upstream's (a16z/jolt#1913, 0xAndoroid/jolt-wasm-prover)

feature: NEAR AI issues the verdict under E2EE v2: the facts go sealed to the attested model key, the model derives the predicates and echoes a binding of the envelope, and `make verify` checks the TDX quote (dcap-qvl, Intel root, committed PCS collateral), report_data (signing key and our nonce), the TEE signature over the exact wire bytes, the sealed answer (opened with its disclosed per-field key), predicates equal to the code's, and the binding
short: NEAR AI issues the verdict under E2EE v2: facts sealed to the attested model key; `make verify` checks the TDX quote and the TEE signature offline
detail: one testnet purchase with a verdict glm-5.3-flash issued (`make model-buy`, 2026-11-05): the facts sealed to the model key registered against its on-chain TDX quote verification, `submit_near_ai_verdict` accepted it (issuer `near-ai:5a0210f2..`), the eval-gated merchant refused it (v4 bucket 50, under 70), m01 settled 36 dUSDC, the replay refused; `make verify-live` re-checks it. one live capture on synthetic facts (chat `08af1d014f2d4f379dba94094562d9ba`, TCB UpToDate). On chain, `submit_near_ai_verdict` accepts it only with a registered model attestation (same nonce), the TEE signature over the exact response bytes, and a sealed answer that opens with the disclosed key and echoes this envelope's binding; `make verify` runs the contract on it and on 4 refusals. The quote check itself happens before `register_model_attestation`, not in the contract; the NVIDIA GPU evidence is checked offline from NVIDIA's signed NRAS reply (`scripts/nras.mjs`)

feature: OutLayer worker as referee: signed result (<= 900 bytes) checked by the contract with `ed25519_verify`; `settle` requires the receipt
detail: in `make verify`; not deployed to OutLayer yet (the register step waits on a founder OK). Live `estimate_execution_cost` = 0.0070001 NEAR

feature: World ID "one person, one agent": the contract checks a verifier's ed25519 attestation and binds one agent per World nullifier; `world_id_human` needs it
detail: on testnet with a placeholder action and our verifier key; the live World ID service (rep-world-verify) is not wired

feature: sealed reviews (Semaphore v4): a settled purchase joins the merchant's group (LeanIMT, Poseidon on chain); during a round a member posts a sealed rating with a Groth16 proof checked on `alt_bn128` host functions, one per member per round (nullifier scoped to merchant and round); after the round members reveal, only if the group has k >= 5 and the round holds at least 5 distinct raters (k_d, since 2026-11-12); release is batched and sorted by hash; `best_quote` breaks price ties by the score and takes a `min_score` floor
short: sealed reviews (Semaphore v4): a buyer who paid rates anonymously, a Groth16 proof is checked on chain, ratings open only at 5 members and 5 raters a round
detail: 3 rounds of 6 sealed ratings released on testnet (2 for m01, 1 for h05); 13 contract tests on real Semaphore proofs

feature: conserved delegation: standing flows from a merchant's released ratings along hire edges to the sub-agents it hires (w = 1/2), following a design rule in REP's draft "(an unpublished REP draft)": the whole chain gets at most w/(1-w) of the seed
short: conserved delegation: standing flows from a merchant's ratings along hire edges at 1/2, capped for the whole chain
detail: standing flowed from m01's released ratings to m02 and m03 on testnet; property test over random graphs with rings

feature: verifiable compute (Jolt zkVM), four guests: standing graph, price stack, referee, cohort k >= 5. The contract keeps the graph root and per-cohort roots; for the graph, the contract keeps a hash-chained root of the standing graph and accepts a score update only when it names the registered program hash, is for the current root and is signed by a bonded worker key that verified the proof off chain. The contract verifies no proof, so it cannot itself tell which program produced the scores
short: Jolt zkVM, four guests (standing graph, price, referee, cohort). The contract verifies no proof: a bonded worker key signs that it did
detail: all four guests proved and verified (prove 1.3 to 9 s, verify about 60 ms, proofs 80 to 93 KB); standing proved twice over the live graph and posted on testnet

detail: (a model, assumptions stated)

detail: four sealed purchases on testnet (38.40 dUSDC twice on synthetic facts; 28 in the `make prove-me` and `make try` pipeline tests); `make verify-live` checks that their txs, events and records carry no predicate, tier or cap; 6 contract and 3 worker tests. `make prove-me` uses this path; the phone run is parked (not in this public copy)

feature: `make prove-me`: your own GitHub account as the real fact. Authenticated `api.github.com/user` notarized with MPC-TLS through the REP notary (pinned key, not attested), 3 fields revealed, the facts sealed to NEAR AI (E2EE v2), a sealed verdict, a `github_builder` line that wins a blind round, one dUSDC settle, `make leak` before and after

detail: the whole pipeline ran live once as a test on a public profile (no token, so a fact about an account, not ownership): builders won `builder-1` at 28 dUSDC (36 without the builder line), `make verify-live` re-checks it; the run on your own `/user` waits on a token; 4 tests

short: Verdict Gate: a Sputnik DAO grants a role to an agent whose verdict reveals a predicate; the DAO opts in by its own proposal
detail: `gate.bookerbob.testnet` with two consumer DAOs (`lisbon-travellers`: airbnb_frequent, `one-human`: world_id_human), one member admitted to each; refused on chain: another agent's verdict, a reused verdict, a sealed verdict; both DAOs' council is REP's; 3 unit tests, `make verify-live`

feature: base-price anchor: a merchant's base is capped at a public price from a named source (`set_price_anchor`), so a discount off an inflated base is refused; unit economics per purchase from measured testnet gas and storage
short: base-price anchor: a merchant's base is capped at a public price from a named source, so a discount off an inflated base is refused
detail: 8 Lisbon hotels capped at their public JMPR rates on testnet; `make cheat`: h05 raising 510 to 600 refused on chain; 4 contract tests (`an_inflated_base_is_refused`); one purchase costs about 0.0102 NEAR in gas and compute plus 0.016 NEAR storage, against a 1% fee; hoodie merchants are not anchored

feature: proven standing tree: the bazaar builds one root from the score list of a Jolt-proven, challengeable graph update and stores no scores; a merchant proves "rank r of n" against it, so the chain answers "is X in the top N%" (`in_top`)
short: proven standing tree: one root on chain, no scores stored; a merchant proves its rank, so the chain answers "is X in the top N%"
detail: live graph of 6 events (hires, m01's two review rounds, h05's first: its 5 group-treasury buyers and the hotel buyer joined its review group), proved in Jolt (zk/out/standing-testnet-3), submitted, unchallenged, finalized: m01 rank 1, h05 rank 2; in_top(m01, 50%) true, h05 on m01's path refused; apply refuses a list that differs from the proven scores hash (test); salts come from the graph root because the scores follow from public events: a rank check, not score privacy

feature: post-quantum: the sealed referee input is hybrid (X25519 + ML-KEM-768, v1 default), every small-domain hash on chain carries a 256-bit salt, and the README states per piece what holds against a quantum attacker
short: post-quantum: the sealed referee input is hybrid (X25519 + ML-KEM-768); the README says per piece what holds and what does not
detail: v1 sealing tests (round trip, swapped KEM ciphertext, downgrade), the contract checks a v1 input's 1,088-byte KEM ciphertext; brute-force tests on the commitment, claims and proof hashes; signatures and Jolt (BN254) are still classical

feature: the NEAR AI model's TDX quote verified on chain: Intel DCAP checks (a dcap-qvl fork) in five calls, and the bazaar registers a model key only against a finalized verification whose report_data is that key and nonce
short: the NEAR AI model's TDX quote verified on chain (Intel DCAP, five calls); the bazaar registers a model key only against that result
detail: five calls of 40, 100, 99, 132 and 69 Tgas; a quote with one changed byte fails at finalize; the bazaar's model key registered through it; the same verification for another key refused; the old off-chain path closed; the verifier account keeps REP's key; the GPU evidence is checked off chain (NRAS)

feature: buying groups on sealed intents: World-bound buyers who revealed the same predicates pool for a fixed-tier discount (10% at 5 persons, 20% at 10); budgets stay committed; each member pays one amount
short: buying groups on sealed intents: World-bound buyers with the same predicates pool for a fixed-tier discount (10% at 5, 20% at 10)
detail: one group of 5 on testnet paid the 10% tier; 8 contract tests

feature: trust anchors under a DAO and a timelock: a Sputnik DAO owns a test bazaar (one council vote is refused, two apply); every anchor change (issuers, model keys, referee, arbiters, World verifier, arbiter threshold, fee, Jolt program, a lower TCB floor) is queued for a public delay, executable by anyone after it and cancellable inside it
short: trust anchors under a DAO and a timelock: every anchor change is queued for a public delay; a Sputnik DAO owns a test bazaar
detail: on `bookerbob-dao-bazaar.testnet` (5 min delay; an early execute refused, a later one applied); 7 + 5 contract tests. The live `bookerbob.testnet` still has one owner key, delay 0, and its full-access key can redeploy the code

short: a buying group's own treasury: a Sputnik DAO per group; only a passed proposal refunds a member or pays the merchant
detail: `lisbon-g1.sputnikv2.testnet`: 6 World-bound hotel buyers, h05's 10% offer (367.20 each), one dropout refunded by proposal, 5 pledges released to h05 by a second proposal (1817.64 dUSDC after the 1% fee), a direct release refused; 6 contract tests

feature: market fee into a DAO treasury: at most 2%, taken from the price (merchant + fee = price), in the liability record, given back on a failed payout, swept by anyone to the treasury; a raise waits out the anchor timelock
short: market fee into a DAO treasury: at most 2%, taken from the merchant's side of the price; a raise waits out the timelock
detail: 1% on testnet, swept to the Sputnik DAO `bookerbob-gov.sputnikv2.testnet`; 5 contract tests

feature: certified private eval (the envelope's second use): a model answers a sealed 20-item set on NEAR AI Cloud, each answer's TEE signature is checked, code grades, a registered issuer signs the certificate; the bazaar stores the floored score and answers `eval_passes(subject, set, threshold)`
short: certified private eval: a model answers a sealed 20-item set on NEAR AI Cloud, code grades, the bazaar stores the certified score
detail: glm-5.3-flash scored 20/20 (bucket 100) on testnet; the items stay private; 5 contract tests

feature: REP Eval, calibrated: 120 sealed items at 4 levels, 3 NEAR AI models in a 400-token budget, every answer TEE-signed, grading and a bootstrap 95% CI in the worker's code, one certificate per model from a separate eval issuer key; a leaderboard page reads the scores from chain
short: REP Eval, calibrated: 120 sealed items, 3 NEAR AI models, every answer TEE-signed, a 95% CI, a leaderboard read from chain
detail: headline on a held-out set made after the protocol was frozen: glm-5.3-flash 58/120 (CI 39.2 to 56.7), DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 112/120, Qwen3.6-35B 0/120 (budget-bound, out of tokens on every item); all 360 TEE signatures valid; the tuned calibration set's run is on chain too and within 3 items; `make eval-verify` in about a second. Only one model lands in the 40 to 80% band. v2 (protocol frozen first): 60 referee-claim items, truth from the referee's code, set committed by its own owner account with `commit_eval_set`: glm 44/60, DeepSeek 35/60, Qwen a budget probe at 0; every answer given was right, every miss a reply cut at 600 tokens; v3, the same items at 2,000 tokens (frozen first): DeepSeek 58/60, glm 55/60, again right on every answer given, so the set is too easy to separate them by accuracy

feature: REP Eval v4 and the eval gate: 40 harder referee-claim items (truth from the referee's code, protocol frozen before the set), and `set_eval_gate`: a merchant sells only to a verdict issued by a NEAR AI model whose certificate passes `eval_passes`
short: REP Eval v4 and the eval gate: a merchant sells only to a verdict from a model whose certificate passes the threshold
detail: v4 on testnet: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 29/40 (bucket 70), glm-5.3-flash 22/40 (bucket 50, the first wrong finished answer in any run); `vetted` gated on v4 at 70 until 2026-11-06 (now the v5 lower bound), an ordinary verdict's receipt was refused on chain; a glm-issued verdict was refused by the gate and bought from m01 instead (`make model-buy`); DeepSeek, its key registered against its on-chain TDX verification, passed under the v4 point-bucket rule and bought from `vetted` (the v5 lower-bound rule would refuse it) (`MODEL_BUY_MODEL=... make model-buy`); the 70 was set after the v4 scores; `make eval-gate`, `make eval-verify`

feature: REP Eval v5: 120 items, protocol committed first, the gate on the Wilson 95% lower bound (threshold 70 fixed before the set), certified apart as `/ci95-lower` with no contract change, truncation reported apart
short: REP Eval v5: 120 items, protocol committed first, the gate on the Wilson 95% lower bound
detail: both bazaars: DeepSeek 91/120 (lower bound 67.4), glm 88/120 (64.8): both in point bucket 70, neither passes 70 on the bound, and `vetted` gates on the bound, so both are refused live (DeepSeek's verdict refused on chain, `make eval-gate`); `make eval-verify` recomputes the bound and reads `eval_passes`

feature: history anchor: NEAR as the history and backup layer for a market that runs on another chain. A contract stores hash-chained round roots from one pinned poster (next seq, previous head, no rewrite, no delete); `make anchor-rebuild` rebuilds the foreign market's groups, members, nullifiers and lists from its own events and checks every root and the chain against NEAR
